headline: Benchmarks Flatter Diagnostic AI; Real Clinical Inputs Tell a Harder Story
subtitle: This week: LLM diagnosis on real inputs, measuring clinician oversight, and audits finding hidden failures
tldr: A Science benchmark puts an AI physician panel at 83.2% on NEJM cases. A preprint finds multi-agent gains reverse on real emergency notes.
Oversight can be measured: in a randomized preprint, clinicians removed 18 of 22 unsupported LLM additions but only 6 of 22 wrong abbreviation expansions.
One ECG-AI 510(k) cleared this week. BMS led Pathos AI's $237M round. Grants went mostly to methods, not to trials of deployed tools.

paper_themes.theme: LLM diagnosis: benchmarks vs real inputs
paper_themes.summary: Strong scores on curated cases sit beside preprints showing text overriding images, overconfidence, and multi-agent gains that reverse on real emergency notes.
Studies move from accuracy to interaction: readers anchoring on AI, errors reviewers miss in AI drafts, directional disagreement metrics, and faster inbox handling.
Skin-tone-dependent labels, skull implants that cannot be implanted, weak OCT grounding, per-patient privacy risk, and digital twins whose accuracy does not track treatment ranking.

top_papers.note: Peer-reviewed benchmark: 83.2% on NEJM cases vs 36.1% for generalist physicians, in a controlled setting only.
Preprint: multi-agent LLM teams improve recall on curated vignettes but reverse on 364 real emergency notes.
Preprint: referral wording swung four multimodal LLMs' glioma-vs-abscess calls far more than the MRI did.
Randomized preprint measures what clinicians catch in LLM discharge drafts; most wrong abbreviation expansions got through.
Erythema was labeled far less often on dark skin (OR 0.17); models trained on these labels repeat the bias.

grants_summary: Mostly VA continuations plus NSF methods awards: PET harmonization, learning under temporal shift, and conformal uncertainty for language models. Few fund prospective evaluation of clinical AI already in use.

top_grants.note: $1.42M to harmonize amyloid and tau PET across sites and tracers, a data foundation for Alzheimer's AI.
VA funds translation of real-time AI diagnosis of colorectal polyps; the VA performs about 300K colonoscopies yearly.
CAREER award on temporal data shift, a main reason deployed health models lose accuracy over time.

products_summary: One AI 510(k) cleared: ECG analysis software (AiTiALVSD). BMS led Pathos AI's $237M round alongside an Alzheimer's deal. FDA launched a neuroscience program. ESMO drug news dominated otherwise.

top_products.note: Another cardiovascular ECG-AI clearance, while evidence on patient outcomes for such tools stays scarce (see spotlight).
Pathos valued at $3B; deal combines a large Tempus dataset, Pathos AI and BMS drug development.
FDA's new NAIN neuroscience program; the announcement does not say what role AI will play.

research_gaps.gap: Diagnostic LLMs not tested on live, messy clinical inputs
research_gaps.evidence: Benchmark used curated CPC and MIMIC cases. Preprints: multi-agent gains reversed on real ED notes, and referral text overrode MRI findings.
research_gaps.suggested_study: Prospective silent-mode study on live ED notes with adjudicated final diagnoses, including arms with misleading referral text.

research_gaps.gap: Unknown which AI error types clinician review actually catches
research_gaps.evidence: Reviewers removed 18/22 unsupported additions but only 6/22 wrong abbreviations. Autoantibody readers' revised ratings almost all moved toward the model.
research_gaps.suggested_study: Seeded-error audits of AI drafting and second-read tools in use, reporting catch rate and anchoring for each error type.

research_gaps.gap: Patient-facing health AI lacks real-user testing outside English
research_gaps.evidence: SIM-UT tested chatbots in India, South Africa and Kenya with simulated users only. Drug-safety warnings weaker in Russian, Arabic and Hebrew Wikipedia.
research_gaps.suggested_study: Prospective multilingual audit of live triage-chatbot conversations, with clinician-rated safety errors by language and literacy.

social.linkedin_post:
BioMed AI Watch, Oct 18–25: benchmarks vs real clinical inputs.

In Science, an AI system that simulates a panel of physicians reached 83.2% accuracy on NEJM clinicopathological cases, compared with 36.1% for generalist physicians. The authors stress this was a controlled benchmark.

Unreviewed preprints this week show what changes outside that setting. Multi-agent LLM teams improved diagnostic recall on curated vignettes but reversed on 364 real emergency department notes. Four multimodal LLMs changed their glioma-vs-abscess calls based on how the referral was worded, far more than based on the MRI.

On oversight, a randomized paediatric discharge study (also a preprint) measured what clinicians caught in LLM drafts. They removed 18 of 22 unsupported additions but only 6 of 22 incorrect abbreviation expansions.

The gap: diagnostic AI needs prospective testing on live clinical inputs, and human review needs metrics broken down by error type.

#ClinicalAI #DigitalHealth
